query: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has high strength at room temperature and elevated temperature but a relatively high density of 10.21 g cm−3. What single intervention could reduce its density without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and at elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C? State the proposed intervention and mechanism, predict directional changes relative to as-cast HfMoTaTiZr, define the applicable temperature and loading boundaries, identify supporting prior evidence, and propose an experiment and rejection criterion that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Substituting a portion of the heavier elements in as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with lighter elements such as Al will reduce the density of the alloy without sacrificing its mechanical properties at room temperature and elevated temperatures, including approximately 1000 °C.
generation.intervention: substitution of heavier elements with lighter ones
generation.conditions: room temperature and elevated temperatures (up to 1000 °C)
generation.predicted_outcome: reduced density by 5-10% relative to the as-cast state
generation.baseline: as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with a density of 10.21 g cm−3
generation.boundary: temperature range up to 1000 °C and loading conditions that do not exceed the yield strength of the alloy
generation.uncertainty: the exact amount of density reduction and the potential effects on mechanical properties may vary depending on the specific substitution and processing conditions

falsification_experiment.design: compare the density and mechanical properties of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr with those of the alloy after substitution with lighter elements
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the density reduction is less than 3% or the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength at room temperature and 1000 °C are reduced by more than 10% relative to the as-cast state, the hypothesis is falsified

cited_evidence.text:
High-entropy alloys (HEAs) can have either high strength or high ductility, and a simultaneous achievement of both still constitutes a tough challenge. The inferior castability and compositional segregation of HEAs are also obstacles for their technological applications. To tackle these problems, here we proposed a novel strategy to design HEAs using the eutectic alloy concept, i.e. to achieve a microstructure composed of alternating soft fcc and hard bcc phases. As a manifestation of this concept, an AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 (atomic portion) eutectic high-entropy alloy (EHEA) was designed. The as-cast EHEA possessed a fine lamellar fcc/B2 microstructure, and showed an unprecedented combination of high tensile ductility and high fracture strength at room temperature. The excellent mechanical properties could be kept up to 700°C. This new alloy design strategy can be readily adapted to large-scale industrial production of HEAs with simultaneous high fracture strength and high ductility.

Abstract This article presents the high temperature tensile and creep behaviors of a novel high entropy alloy (HEA). The microstructure of this HEA resembles that of advanced superalloys with a high entropy FCC matrix and L1 2 ordered precipitates, so it is also named as “high entropy superalloy (HESA)”. The tensile yield strengths of HESA surpass those of the reported HEAs from room temperature to elevated temperatures; furthermore, its creep resistance at 982 °C can be compared to those of some Ni-based superalloys. Analysis on experimental results indicate that HESA could be strengthened by the low stacking-fault energy of the matrix, high anti-phase boundary energy of the strengthening precipitate, and thermally stable microstructure. Positive misfit between FCC matrix and precipitate has yielded parallel raft microstructure during creep at 982 °C, and the creep curves of HESA were dominated by tertiary creep behavior. To the best of authors’ knowledge, this article is the first to present the elevated temperature tensile creep study on full scale specimens of a high entropy alloy, and the potential of HESA for high temperature structural application is discussed.
